initial_prompt: Explain quantum entanglement like I'm 5 years old.

messages.content: Explain quantum entanglement like I'm 5 years old.

Okay, here's how I'd explain it:

---

Imagine you have two magic socks. You put one in your backpack and give one to your friend, and your friend goes really far away - like to grandma's house.

Here's the weird part: when you look at your sock and see it's red, you *instantly* know your friend's sock is blue. Always. Even before anyone tells you, even before your friend looks at theirs.

It's like the socks are playing a secret game together, and they always give opposite answers, no matter how far apart they are.

The really strange thing that grown-ups are still figuring out? The socks don't seem to "decide" what color they are until someone actually looks. But somehow they still always match up as opposites.

Nobody peeked. Nobody cheated. They just... know about each other, even across the whole world.

---

That's kind of what entanglement is like. Two tiny tiny things - way smaller than socks - that stay connected in this spooky way, even when they're super far apart.

Scientists think it's one of the weirdest and coolest things in the whole universe. And honestly? They're still figuring out exactly *why* it works.
